claims.statement: The project registers exactly 15 modules in settings.gradle.kts (:app, :core:model, :core:common, :core:ui, :core:skin, :domain, :data, :player, six :feature:* modules, :benchmark), which is the same list ProductArchitectureVerification requires; each module must keep a .gitignore with /build/, /.cxx/, /.externalNativeBuild/, /captures/.

Feature modules may depend only on :core:model, :core:common, :core:ui and :domain; no feature build file declares project(":data"), project(":player") or another project(":feature:..."), and ProductArchitectureVerification fails any build file that adds them, so cross-feature navigation must be routed through :app.

:player and :data are symmetric middle layers that each depend only on :core:model, :core:common and :domain (plus platform libraries such as Media3, Room, DataStore and Hilt); neither depends on the other or on any feature module.

:domain contains no Android or Compose dependencies at all (no file under domain/src/main/java imports android.* or androidx.*); it api-exposes :core:model and implementation-depends on :core:common, making it a pure interface/policy layer.

:core:model is the dependency-free bottom layer holding pure data types (Song, Playlist, PlayQueue, AlbumEntry, ArtistEntry, LyricLine, SongInfo, SongEmotion, TimeSlotConfig, ThemeMode/ThemeVariant); its only external dependency is compose-runtime for @Stable/@Immutable annotations, and Song itself stores an android.net.Uri.

:app is the only module that depends on every other module (:core:*, :domain, :data, :player and all six features); AppNavHost.kt is the single composition point that wires feature Route composables together, so no feature renders another feature's UI.

Hilt product assembly is anchored at four verified entry points: MelodyApplication (@HiltAndroidApp), MainActivity (@AndroidEntryPoint), AppMediaSessionService in :player (@AndroidEntryPoint), and PlayerViewModel in :feature:player (@HiltViewModel); the gate checks each file keeps its annotation.

Six SingletonComponent Hilt modules are enforced by the gate (app/di CoroutineModule, LoggerModule, PlayerModule; data/di DatabaseModule, DataStoreModule, RepositoryModule), plus player's AppCoroutineScopeModule, which provides the @ApplicationScope process-level CoroutineScope so playback-snapshot persistence survives service destruction.

Repository implementations follow a narrow-adapter pattern: MusicRepository is an internal storage coordinator that implements none of the domain repository interfaces; RepositoryModule binds each :domain interface to a dedicated adapter class (SongRepositoryAdapter, PlaylistRepositoryAdapter, MusicImportRepositoryAdapter, AlbumArtRepositoryAdapter) that delegates to it, with MediaMetadataRepository serving both LyricsRepository and SongMetadataRepository.

ProductArchitectureVerification enforces the adapter pattern in both directions: imports of cn.com.dcsgo.mihx.data.repository.* or cn.com.dcsgo.mihx.data.local.* are banned in feature/, domain/ and player/ sources, MusicRepository must not declare SongRepository/PlaylistRepository/MusicImportRepository/AlbumArtRepository as supertypes, and the four *RepositoryAdapter.kt files must exist and implement their named domain interface.

app/di/PlayerModule is the binding point for all playback Ports declared in :domain's cn.com.dcsgo.mihx.domain.playback package: ControllerQueuePlannerPort, PlaybackControllerPortFactory, PlaybackStateStorageFactory, PlaybackStateRepository, BluetoothPlaybackMonitorFactory, PlaybackDurationMonitorFactory and PlayerQueueServicesFactory.

:feature:player consumes the ports through PlayerRuntimeFactory, whose constructor injects ControllerQueuePlannerPort, PlaybackControllerPortFactory, PlaybackStateStorageFactory, BluetoothPlaybackMonitorFactory, PlaybackDurationMonitorFactory and PlayerQueueServicesFactory (plus the TimeSlotConfigRepository, SongEmotionRepository and WordPreferenceRepository contracts) and passes them into PlayerRuntime; e.g. PlayerControllerQueueFacade builds windowed sync plans solely via the ControllerQueuePlannerPort abstraction.

The :player module supplies WindowedControllerQueuePlanner (in player/window/) as the ControllerQueuePlannerPort implementation; it delegates to ControllerWindowSynchronizer.planControllerQueue, keeping the window algorithm dependent only on :core:model and :domain playback policy.

PlaybackStateStore in :player is a single class that implements both the :domain PlaybackStateStorage port and PlaybackStateRepository interface; PlayerModule provides it as the singleton storage and hands it out through both factories, backed by the playback_state DataStore with legacy SharedPreferences fallback.

PlaybackControllerPortFactory creates PlaybackController bound to AppMediaSessionService::class.java, so the Media3 playback control path is UI -> PlaybackControllerPort -> PlaybackController (MediaController client, FIFO pending-action cap 64) -> AppMediaSessionService (MediaSessionService owning ExoPlayer), all cross-module edges via :domain abstractions.

The rule engine behind verifyProductArchitecture was extracted (2026-10-15) into ProductArchitectureVerification.verify(rootDir) in buildSrc, a unit-testable pure function that walks all kt/kts/java/xml/toml files (excluding build/.gradle/.git/.idea/buildSrc dirs) and returns the collected list of violations; the root verifyProductArchitecture task (group verification) throws GradleException only when the list is non-empty, and root check depends on spotlessCheck, verifyProductArchitecture and every subproject's check.

The release-build rule extracts the :app release block with a brace-pairing parser (extractBracedBlock) that survives nested braces/lambdas inside the block, replacing the old first-closing-brace regex; the rule still asserts isMinifyEnabled = true and isShrinkResources = true in that block.

Room schema history is immutability-checked: 1.json must not contain quick_skip_short_play_counts, 2.json must contain it but not lrcUri, 3.json must contain lrcUri; MelodyMigrations must keep Migration(1,2) and Migration(2,3), and DatabaseModule must register them via addMigrations(*MelodyMigrations.ALL).

The exported schema history runs through 17.json: MelodyDatabase declares version = 17 with 14 entities (WordPreferenceEntity added in the 10->11 migration that creates the word_preferences table), migrations from 1->2 through 16->17 are registered via the MelodyMigrations.ALL array, and MIGRATION_16_17 adds the missing index_songs_albumId and index_playback_events_songId indexes; the standing rule is to add new snapshots/migrations, never edit existing schema JSON files.

Both app/src/main/res/xml/backup_rules.xml and data_extraction_rules.xml must exclude the privacy-sensitive stores (legacy prefs music_player_prefs/play_stats_prefs/quick_skip_songs_prefs, melody.db plus -journal/-shm/-wal, datastore/player_settings.preferences_pb, datastore/playback_state.preferences_pb, cache/album_art/); missing entries fail the build.

The gate fixes release build shape: :app release must set isMinifyEnabled = true and isShrinkResources = true, a benchmark build type must exist with initWith(getByName("release")), and the :app manifest must not declare AppMediaSessionService (it lives in the :player manifest) nor request READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE (SAF document-tree import). READ_MEDIA_AUDIO is allowed: it accelerates import via java.io.File direct traversal when granted, with SAF as the primary path and fallback.

Code-quality gates include: every LazyColumn item/items/itemsIndexed call in app, core and feature sources must pass a stable key, and direct android.util.Log calls are banned everywhere except AppLogger.kt in favor of AppLog/AppLogger (which redact URIs/paths in release).

Privacy-sensitive startup rules are enforced: Bluetooth playback monitoring must be user-triggered from Settings (PlayerStartupFacade must not mention Bluetooth; SettingsScreen must expose the 蓝牙播放监听/申请蓝牙权限 controls; the setting must flow through PlayerSettingsRepository/DataStore into PlayerUiState, not app-shell remember state), and startup-path files (MainActivity, AppRoot, PlayerRuntime, PlayerStartupFacade) must not request notification or Bluetooth permissions.

Observability anchors are enforced: MusicRepository must keep the music_import_scan and music_import_folder PerformanceTrace operations and PlaybackController the controller_play_queue/controller_prepare_queue/controller_sync_queue/play_next_command operations; PlaybackWindowPerformanceShapeTest must keep covering 100/500/1_000/71-song window sizing; :benchmark must remain a Macrobenchmark module targeting :app with a StartupBenchmark using MacrobenchmarkRule, StartupTimingMetric and StartupMode.COLD.
Every required module must keep a local .gitignore containing /build/, /.cxx/, /.externalNativeBuild/ and /captures/; the gate reports every module whose ignore file is missing or incomplete.

The port indirection keeps :feature:player logic unit-testable off-device: PlayerControllerQueueFacadeTest substitutes a hand-written fake ControllerQueuePlannerPort instead of any Media3 or :player implementation.

:core:skin (namespace cn.com.dcsgo.mihx.core.skin) is a bottom-layer core module depending only on :core:model (for ThemeVariant) and org.json; it carries no Android resources, no R.* ids and no Compose runtime, so a skin description is headlessly parseable and unit-testable. It is consumed only by :app and :feature:user.

A skin is never executable code: it is a JSON description the host uses to assemble existing parts, so import carries zero composition-time crash risk. SkinParser validates fail-closed — unknown part names are rejected (never silently downgraded) via the SkinPartCatalog whitelist, unknown fields are ignored for forward compatibility, out-of-range tokens are clamped as warnings, schema version must equal 1, and validation returns all issues at once through the SkinValidation sealed type.

The mapping from skin description symbols to host artifacts lives in :app, not :core:skin: SkinShellResolver maps page keys to routes (library→AppRoutes.PLAYLIST, player→AppRoutes.HOME, me→AppRoutes.USER) and part/icon names to drawables, keeping :core:skin free of routing and android.resource knowledge; the runtime AppShell and the SharedPreferences-backed SkinSwitcherStore also live in :app.

:feature:user hosts the partitioned "我的" page metadata: UserSections part names (userInfo/playStats/moodTimeSlot/emotionScan/fileCheck/skinSwitcher) must match SkinPartCatalog constants, cross-checked by UserSectionsMatchDescriptionTest; :feature:user is the only feature module that depends on :core:skin. :feature:playlist hosts the library sorting helpers SongSorter and SortModeDropdownMenu.

Explore playback (v3.11.0) is a domain-policy feature split across the boundaries: :domain owns ExplorePlaybackPolicy (INITIAL_BATCH_SIZE = 10, REFILL_COUNT = 5, REFILL_THRESHOLD = 0, MIN_LISTEN_MS = 30_000L / MIN_LISTEN_RATIO = 0.25f defining a quick skip, plus VOTE_MIN_RATIO/VOTE_MAX_TAGS/VOTE_WEIGHT_SCALE for proportional voting) and RandomQueuePlanner; :feature:player owns PlayerRandomQueueFacade.playRandomQueue/refillExplorePlayQueue/buildExploreRefillPool with a layered candidate pool (liked & no-dislike, then no-dislike, then full library), which applies votes through the WordPreferenceRepository contract; :data persists votes via WordPreferencesRepository (Room word_preferences) using per-word atomic SQL increments (ensureWordPreference + addWordVotesDelta, M-22) so concurrent skip/full-listen settlements never lose a vote, weighted by the word's proportion in the song (x100 scale, historical votes rescaled in MIGRATION_15_16).

Emotion analysis memory is budgeted adaptively to the device heap: both EmotionAnalyzer and FfmpegPcmDecoder read memoryBudgetBytes = EmotionAnalyzer.memoryBudgetForHeap(Runtime.getRuntime().maxMemory()), which returns (maxHeap - 64MB baseline reservation) clamped into [96MB, 512MB]; a 256MB heap yields 192MB (unchanged behavior on low-end devices), while larger heaps (384MB -> 320MB, 512MB -> 448MB) automatically allow longer 192 kHz files. ShortAccum trims truncation during decode and truncationReason distinguishes 'too long' from 'memory exceeded'.

:player classes live under cn.com.dcsgo.mihx.player (migrated from the old cn.com.dcsgo.mihx.data.player package so the package matches the module namespace); the architecture gate rejects any remaining cn.com.dcsgo.mihx.data.player reference in :player sources to prevent regression.

The M-21 gate rule (2026-10-27) bans new `import android.*` in :core:model and :domain on a ratchet basis: pre-existing Android-framework imports are whitelisted in a baseline (android.net.Uri in Song/AlbumEntry/ArtistEntry, and FolderImporter/MusicImportRepository in :domain), so they compile today but any new Android-framework import in those two layers fails the build; the Uri->String migration that would clear the baseline has not happened yet.

:data declares the album-art FileProvider in its manifest with authority `${applicationId}.artworkprovider` and an `@xml/artwork_file_paths` path mapping, exposing cacheDir/album_art as content:// URIs for cross-process consumers (notifications/SystemUI/Android Auto); the authority uses `${applicationId}` rather than a hardcoded package so the debug variant's `<package>.debug` applicationId still resolves, and the gate forbids the :app manifest from declaring AppMediaSessionService in the same manifest.
